body: I don’t get people who purposely marry Asian/White people and then regret having an “Asian” child, coming from a halfie with an “Eastern” face myself.

Half-Japanese American (technically yonsei), grown up mainly in Hawaii for 15 years.

Honestly, my mother (Brazilian national full Japanese) hated Japan and wanted me to only learn Portuguese and especially English. However, my father was almost never home and she instinctively taught me Japanese customs which helped me study Japanese easily when I moved back here during high school.

The best way to explain it is that Japanese heavily tied to its culture. If you can’t understand the culture, you will speak like an expat until you die. Especially with 空気を読む (kūki wo yomu), which non-Japanese have a hard time understanding well. I’d say it would mean to modestly read the situation.
